panchanga.chandrabalam_thaaraabalam_note: ROUND-10 (review P2-4): in PyJHora 5.0 drik.chandrabalam(jd, place) and drik.thaaraabalam(jd, place, return_only_good_stars=True) take NO moon_raasi / nakshatra keyword — the proposed natal-specific call signature does not exist in this build, so it was not adopted. Both are MUHURTA helpers evaluated at the query jd (chandrabalam lists favourable ascendant windows for the CURRENT Moon's sign; thaaraabalam lists good nakshatras for that day). Natal-relative equivalents already in this document: panchanga.nava_thaara_from_moon (the 9-tara cycle from the NATAL Moon nakshatra), panchanga.nava_thaara_from_lagna, and transits.moon.transit_house_from_moon (the count from the natal Moon that drives chandrabalam/tara-bala judgement in gochara).

thaaraabalam.__note__: MUHURTA helper: natal-stars (1..27) that have a good tara vs TODAY's Moon star (Paramitra/Sampatha/Kshema/Sadhana/Mitra). Not natal tara-bala.

combustion_detail.__note__: ROUND-11 (review P2-1): standard BPHS combustion orbs — Moon 12, Mars 17, Mercury 14 (retrograde 12), Jupiter 11, Venus 10 (retrograde 8), Saturn 15 degrees from the Sun, measured as the minimal arc (wrap-aware); cazimi = within 0 deg 17 min (0.2833), the heart zone where a combust planet is read as fully empowered rather than weakened. planet_flags.combust and core.planets[].is_combust remain the LIBRARY verdict (charts.planets_in_combustion: mis-indexed orb table at planet_id-2 + stale chart-layer retrograde check — upstream quirk disclosed, not refixed); library_vs_standard_mismatch marks bodies where the two verdicts differ. Worked example (sample chart): retrograde Mercury at 16.07 deg — library 'combust' (using Mars's 17 deg orb), standard NOT combust (Mercury retrograde orb is 12 deg). Prefer combust_per_standard_orb for readings; cite both verdicts when they diverge.

planet_flags.graha_yudh_note: Empty list = no planetary war at birth. A graha-yudh pair mutually afflicts both planets' significations.

avasthas.__note__: Baaladi: 6-degree bands; odd signs Bala(0-6)→Mrita(24-30), even signs reversed; result percents are the conventional BPHS-lineage strengths (Bala 25%, Kumara 50%, Yuva 100%, Vriddha 12.5%, Mrita 0% — some texts give Vriddha 25%). Jagradadi: Jagrita=own/exalted, Sushupti=debilitated or enemy-of-sign-lord (compound relationship), else Swapna. Rahu/Ketu use the odd-sign rule.

gandanta.__note__: ROUND-11 (review P2-2): gandanta = the 'knot' at water->fire sign junctions — last 3d20m of Cancer/Scorpio/Pisces + first 3d20m of Aries/Leo/Sagittarius (exactly one pada; nakshatra gandanta — Revati, Ashlesha, Jyeshtha pada 4 — coincides with the water-side zone). Bodies here are read as intense, unstable, karmically pressurized until the exact junction is crossed (degrees_to_exact_junction measures the distance to that point). Deterministic degree arithmetic — no library API. Nakshatra/tithi gandanta (solar-lunar junction TIMINGS) are not computed; this is degree gandanta only.

dual_sign_rulers.__note__: Jaimini dual-signature resolution via house.stronger_planet_from_planet_positions (library rule chain; check_during_dhasa=False). Parashari sign lordship is unaffected: Scorpio=Mars, Aquarius=Saturn everywhere else in this document (core.houses[].sign_lord etc.).

manglik.note: reference = lagna, 2nd house included (South-Indian convention); library-exact semantics (ROUND-13 correction): 'present' is the house-rule verdict from the apply_exceptions=True call — the library REPORTS BV Raman cancellations ALONGSIDE the verdict ('exceptions_applied'/'exception_indices') WITHOUT flipping the boolean; 'present_before_exceptions' is the raw-call verdict (identical by library design). ROUND-13: see manglik_multi_reference for the Moon/Venus frames.

manglik_multi_reference.__note__: ROUND-13 (review item 5): Kuja/Manglik dosha evaluated from ALL THREE classical reference frames using the LIBRARY's own manglik_reference_planet parameter ('L' lagna / 1 Moon / 5 Venus) — no reimplementation. Library-exact semantics: 'present' is the house-rule verdict (the library's apply_exceptions REPORTS BV Raman cancellations alongside the verdict via 'exceptions_applied'/'exception_indices' WITHOUT flipping the boolean); 'present_before_exceptions' is the raw-call verdict. House set: library default [2, 4, 7, 8, 12] (South-Indian 2nd-house inclusion; the 1st house excluded per the library's Sanjay Rath citation — 'lagna house not in ancient text'); the review's (1,2,4,7,8,12) union is exposed as present_with_lagna_house_raw. READERS: after lagna, the Moon-reference is the most widely used classical check; a dosha present from one frame but absent in another is a PARTIAL dosha — report the verdict per frame TOGETHER with its active BV Raman exception indices (where exceptions are active, many texts treat the dosha as cancelled or weakened — an interpretation call, disclosed not automated), and cross-check the partner via match.manglik_compatibility (lagna frame, identical library calls).

karakas.nak_karaka_definition: 0=Surya,1=Chandra,2=Mangala,3=Budha,4=Guru,5=Sukra,6=Sani,7=Rahu (8-karaka scheme; Ketu is excluded as it always owns the 7th/8th kendra and is not a Jaimini karaka). Roles assigned in DECREASING degree order — Rahu is ranked by (30° - its degree-in-sign), the library/JHora mirror convention for the shadow planet — so the Darakaraka (spouse) is the LAST body in the list.

yogini_decoded.__note__: ROUND-12 (review F5): decoded view of the raw dasha.yogini rows ([lords, start, duration]). The 8 yoginis — Mangala (Moon, 1y), Pingala (Sun, 2y), Dhanya (Jupiter, 3y), Bhramari (Mars, 4y), Bhadrika (Mercury, 5y), Ulka (Saturn, 6y), Siddha (Venus, 7y), Sankata (Rahu, 8y); 36-year cycle — come from the library's own yogini.dhasa_adhipathi_list (lords + durations); the classical NAMES are wrapper-provided (web-verified, unanimous across sources). Lords tuples decode mahadasha first, then antardasha. DURATIONS ARE THE LIBRARY'S: this build splits every mahadasha into 8 EQUAL antardashas (MD_years/8); some classical texts prescribe PROPORTIONAL antardashas (MD × yogini_years/36) — disclosed, not recomputed. Yogini is the fast 36-year cycle used for quick event timing (Nadi/traditional lineages); vimsottari remains the engine's tone authority.

Zone semantics per the library's own captions: Exterior / Wall / Interior / Pillar. Classical reading (outer rings = distant/mild effects, inner = immediate/intense) is interpretive doctrine, NOT computed by the library.

sarvatobhadra_chakra.__note__: DATA PORT of jhora/ui/chakra.py Sarvatobadra._grid_label_values (hardcoded 9x9): border integers = nakshatras 1-28 (Abhijit included), interior integers = rasis 1-12, strings = vowel/consonant syllables plus the five tithi-group cells with their weekday pairings (Nanda Sun/Tue, Bhadra Mon/Wed, Jaya Thu, Rikita Fri, Pooma Sat); planet cells resolve via drik.nakshatra_pada exactly as the widget does. DISCLOSURE: PyJHora computes NO vedha (obstruction/penetration) relationships for this chakra anywhere in the library - the review's 'vedha penetrations' are NOT a missing extraction; the vedha rules are classical doctrine the interpreter applies to this grid data.

saturn_gochara_from_natal_moon.conventions: Sade Sati = Saturn transiting the 12th/1st/2nd from the NATAL MOON (rising/peak/setting phases). Ashtama Shani = 8th. Kantaka (thorn) = 4th/7th/10th per common usage. Ardhashtama ('half of the 8th') = 4th from the natal Moon — it coincides with Kantaka and is classically rated about half as severe as Ashtama. Saturn in the 5th (Panchama) is flagged separately and is not ardhashtama. house_from_natal_moon is the authoritative number.

jupiter_gochara_from_natal_moon.conventions: Jupiter transiting the 2nd/5th/7th/9th/11th from the natal Moon is conventionally auspicious (some texts add the 4th); the 8th/12th are conventionally difficult.

transits.kakshya_transits_note: ROUND-11 (review P2-4): each transits[] row for Sun..Saturn carries a kakshya block — the 3d45m sub-sign division of the transit sign, whose lords from 0 deg are Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Lagna. Classical rule: the kakshya is FAVORABLE for the transiting planet iff the kakshya lord contributed a bindu to that sign in the transiting planet's OWN natal prastara/BAV row (natal_bindu_from_kakshya_lord_at_transit_sign = 1). Rahu/Ketu rows have no kakshya block — the nodes have no BAV row. Wrapper-computed (no PyJHora kakshya API exists); doctrine web-verified across five independent sources.
transits.latta_stars_note: Per natal planet: the two nakshatras whose lunar transit afflicts that planet (classical latta-star rule).
